title: An Integrated Approach to Tuition Refund Protection for Private K–12 Schools
summary: Building on the previously announced partnership, Blackbaud today announced that its integration with Vertical Insure is now live in the Blackbaud Marketplace
body_text: Blackbaud is continuing to evolve how private K–12 school customers can offer tuition refund protection through an expanded integration with Vertical Insure Building on the previously announced partnership , Blackbaud today announced that its integration with Vertical Insure is now live in the Blackbaud Marketplace . Schools can go into the Blackbaud Marketplace and can get started today to enable it for the upcoming 27-28 enrollment year. As the offering evolves, it will be embedded directly into contracts within Blackbaud Enrollment Management, making it even easier for schools to adopt without added complexity. The Vertical Insure integration is built into Blackbaud’s K–12 Enrollment Management System through its integrated contracts with both Tuition Management and Billing Management, shifting tuition protection from a standalone insurance process to a platform-native part of how tuition is structured and managed. The result is a simpler experience for schools and families, without the administrative burden that has traditionally made tuition protection difficult to offer. “Schools shouldn’t have to manage complex insurance processes alongside everything else they do,” said Mark Davis, vice president and head of education products, Blackbaud. “By embedding tuition refund protection directly into our Tuition Management, Billing Management, and Enrollment Management solutions, and expanding access through the Blackbaud Marketplace, we’re removing that burden and making it easier for schools to offer valuable protection as a seamless part of the experience.” Built Into the Way Schools Already Operate For many schools, tuition refund protection has historically required a separate enrollment process, manual tracking, and ongoing coordination with insurance providers. These legacy approaches often divert staff time and introduce added complexity, especially for schools managing tuition through payment plans. By embedding tuition refund protection directly into Blackbaud’s platform, those barriers are removed. Schools can now offer—or require—coverage as part of existing tuition payment plans, with protection presented at the moment families commit to tuition. Families do not have to leave the platform or complete additional steps, creating a more seamless and transparent experience. No Added Administrative Work Because the solution is fully integrated, schools are no longer responsible for managing insurance administration. There is no separate enrollment or contract management, no manual policy tracking, and no reconciliation required. Insurance operations are handled behind the scenes, allowing schools to offer tuition refund protection without introducing additional workflows or staff burden. This approach makes tuition protection accessible not only to larger institutions, but also to smaller schools that may not have previously offered coverage due to operational constraints. “Tuition refund protection doesn’t have to create more work,” said Brock Noland, CEO of Vertical Insure. “Our partnership with Blackbaud makes it possible for schools of any size to offer coverage without the complexity of establishing or managing a separate insurance program.” Stronger, More Consistent Coverage Tuition Refund Protection powered by Vertical Insure is designed to cover up to 100% of eligible tuition for covered reasons, helping protect both family investment and school revenue. Unlike traditional models that can vary significantly based on individual school agreements, this approach offers a more consistent and transparent coverage structure. Schools also benefit from a model that is typically more cost effective and avoids the variability commonly associated with legacy tuition protection programs. Why This Matters for K 12 Private and Independent Schools This expansion reflects a broader shift toward platform led solutions in K 12 education — where essential services are delivered within the systems schools already rely on, rather than layered on through separate vendors and processes. By aligning tuition refund protection with how tuition is billed, managed, and paid, Blackbaud is helping schools simplify operations while expanding access to coverage for more families. For Blackbaud customers, tuition protection becomes less of a separate decision and more of a built in capability that supports modern enrollment, billing, and payment plan workflows.

title: Your Spring Gala Is a DAF Fundraising Opportunity You May Be Missing
summary: Spring gala season is here. The tables are set, the paddle raise is rehearsed, and your team is ready. But there's one opportunity most organizations walk right past every single event: their DAF donors.
body_text: Spring gala season is here. The tables are set, the paddle raise is rehearsed, and your team is ready. But there's one opportunity most organizations walk right past every single event: their DAF donors. With $64.9 billion distributed from donor-advised funds in 2024 alone — and $326 billion more ready to grant — your gala attendees are, statistically, holding DAF funds. The question isn't whether DAF donors will be in the room with you on event night. It's whether you'll make it easy for them to give. Start at Check-In The check-in table is the most underutilized DAF touchpoint in nonprofit fundraising. Every attendee stops there. Some hand over a credit card to be on file for auction items or a bar tab. And right there — in that 60-second window — is your chance to start a conversation that changes the entire giving picture for the night. Train your check-in staff to ask one simple question: "Do you use a donor-advised fund? Just so you know, you can't use a DAF for auction items tonight — but you absolutely can for any general donations to the organization, including the paddle raise." That's it. One question, said genuinely, as a service to the donor rather than a pitch. The impact is two-fold: you're helping your supporter show up more intentionally, and you're learning something about their giving preferences that no wealth screening report will ever surface. Don't Just Tell Donors Where They Can't Give Here's a pattern worth breaking: organizations that post "DAFs cannot be used for auction items" disclaimers throughout the silent auction room — but never once mention where donors can use their DAF. When supporters only hear what's off-limits, many simply disengage from DAF giving for the night altogether. The better approach is balance. Acknowledge the restriction, then immediately pivot to the opportunity: here is where your DAF can make an impact tonight. Put signage up during the paddle raise. Mention it in the program. Give your guests a clear, specific answer. Brief Your Auctioneer and Host Your MC has a microphone. Use it. A short announcement from the stage during the fund-a-need or paddle raise moment — "If you give through a donor-advised fund, you can absolutely use it for this" — can meaningfully increase participation. Donors who hadn't thought to use their DAF, or weren't sure they could, will act when they hear it said clearly and confidently from the front of the room. Give your auctioneer two sentences to say and practice it with them before the event. It doesn't take a long script — just clarity. Make It Easy to Give with DAFpay If you have DAFpay enabled on your donation forms, your gala gets even more powerful. Set up a QR code on each table — or display it on the event screen — that links directly to your donation page. When donors reach checkout, DAFpay gives them the option to give straight from their DAF account, the same way they'd swipe a credit card. Your check-in staff and auctioneer can mention it in the same breath: "And if you'd like to use your DAF for a general donation tonight, you can do it right from your phone — just scan the QR code on your table." No pledge cards. No "I'll have my DAF sponsor send a check later." The gift gets made in the moment, while the energy is still high. According to our 2025 DAF Fundraising Report , donors who give with their DAF give 10x more an average compared to other giving methods. If DAFpay isn't yet on your donation forms, gala season is the prompt you've been waiting for. Getting set up before your next event means any donor in the room — not just the ones your team has a chance to speak with — can give the way they prefer. See which fundraising platforms you can use that already have DAFpay integrated. Track What You Learn Check-in conversations create data. Don't let it walk out the door. When a staff member learns a donor has a DAF, that information belongs in your CRM. Even a simple flag — "has DAF" — opens a different cultivation path. You can add them to DAF-specific communications, make sure they hear about DAF Day (October 8, 2026 this year), and reach out in ways that match how they actually prefer to give. Brief your check-in team to capture this. A note in your event app, a post-event data entry task — whatever fits your workflow. The long-term value of a more complete donor file is worth far more than the five minutes it takes. Steward Faster While the Event Is Still Fresh One of the biggest missed opportunities after a gala isn't the gift itself — it's what happens in the days that follow. Donors are most receptive right after an event. The energy is high, the connection is fresh, and a personal acknowledgment lands differently than it would two weeks later. Getting your gift processing done quickly is what makes that window real. With Chariot's gift processing software , your team can reconcile and credit DAF gifts without waiting for checks to arrive or chasing down pledge fulfillments. When a donor gives through DAFpay, their name and email come through with the gift so your team can reach out within the same week, not weeks later. That's the moment to send the handwritten note. The thank-you video. The personal call from your ED. Don't let your operations be the thing that slows down your stewardship. The Takeaway Gala season isn't just an opportunity to raise money — it's an opportunity to learn more about your donors and build habits that will serve your DAF fundraising all year long. Ask at check-in. Say something from the stage. Put the QR code on the table and on the big screen. Process gifts quickly and steward while the event energy is still alive. Your DAF donors are already in the room. All that's left is meeting them where they are. Subscribe to the Chariot newsletter and follow us on LinkedIn for DAF fundraising insights, product updates, and seasonal resources.

title: Engineering C-UAS Systems for Allied Defense
summary: As U.S. and EU data standards redefine C-UAS requirements, explore how Plexus enables mission readiness by transitioning complex prototypes into scalable, interoperable allied assets.
body_text: Home Blogs Engineering C-UAS Systems for Allied Defense Engineering C-UAS Systems for Allied Defense Paul Cahill Sr Engineering Customer Development Manager – Europe • July 23, 2026 • 5 min read Designing Share using Native tools Share Copied to clipboard Share on Mail (Opens in new window) Mail Key Takeaways Discover how a unified hardware partnership eliminates the systemic risks, long lead times, and vendor handoff friction that typically stall complex defense prototypes. Learn the practical engineering mechanics, including Design for Excellence (DFX) and automated assembly, needed to rapidly scale low-cost kinetic and non-kinetic shields. Military interoperability is moving from a high-level ambition to a technical requirement. The recent landmark agreement between the U.S. Department of War (DOW) and the United Kingdom’s Ministry of Defence (MoD) to standardize counter-unmanned aerial system (C-UAS) data represents a fundamental change in how defense technology will be procured and deployed. Innovators now need to achieve total system interoperability while also scaling production to meet the urgent requirements of sovereign defense, anti drone systems, and allied security. With the formalization of the U.S. and UK data standards and the broader push for integrated air defense systems architectures, the requirements for entry have shifted. Success now requires transitioning from a standalone solution to an integrated allied asset. To remain viable in the allied marketplace, counter UAS systems must communicate through common data standards and be engineered for rapid scaling to match the pace of emerging threats. Crossing this barrier requires a trusted partner in aerospace and defense manufacturing equipped to handle complex regulatory, compliance, and technical complexities from day one. The Mandate for Sustainable Defense Readiness The effectiveness of a defensive shield is measured by its reliability and its sustainability. As threats evolve, the ability to deploy protective measures at scale is essential to maintaining national security and deterring conflict. This requirement for industrial readiness is now the primary driver for regional defense mandates across the global aerospace electronics manufacturing landscape: U.S. Replicator Initiative: The U.S. DoD is focused on scaling autonomous systems to ensure mission readiness. This mandate requires OEMs to move toward highly reliable, mass-produced solutions that ensure the nation’s security through industrial strength. Golden Dome & JIATF-401: The UK and U.S. are leveraging Joint Interagency Task Force 401 to ensure that defensive systems are integrated and interoperable. Access to the allied marketplace depends on a system’s ability to operate within a unified shield where sensors and protective effectors work in unison. EU 2026 Action Plan on Counter Drone Security: The European Commission has prioritized a rapid industrial production ramp-up to protect critical infrastructure. This plan calls for fast-tracking reliable C-UAS solutions and dual use technology to secure borders and preserve stability across the region. Engineering Systems for Fleet Readiness Plexus supports the industrialization of these systems by transitioning complex, high-reliability designs into scalable production. Whether the requirement is for high-volume defensive UAS, loitering munitions, or complex, integrated C-UAS platforms, we leverage automated assembly and intense environmental stress screening (HALT and HASS) to ensure every system maintains a constant state of mission readiness in the most contested environments. By applying Design for Excellence (DFX) principles early in the product strategy phase, Plexus engineers identify opportunities to mitigate risk before they become costly scaling challenges. Refining Current Hardware for Mass Production To improve speed-to-market, we focus on removing manufacturing bottlenecks: Touch-Time Reduction: We study the build process to remove manual bottlenecks by standardizing requirements and by removing variability within the build, ensuring that every unit is built the same to the highest quality standard. Quality and Poka-Yoke Integration: We implement physical error-proofing features to ensure parts can only be assembled in the correct orientation, practically eliminating human error during production. Part Consolidation (DFA): We re-engineer early concepts to reduce the number of unique components, replacing complex multi-part housings with consolidated mechanical configurations to maximize production throughput. Embedding Engineering in Evolving Designs For next-generation protective payloads, Plexus embeds manufacturing intelligence before the design freezes: Design for Assembly (DFA) from Day One: We ensure enclosures allow for logical assembly sequencing to maximize production efficiency. Tolerance Stack-Up Analysis: Our technical teams provide rigorous analysis to ensure all components mate perfectly on the first build, ensuring the integrity of the protective system. Design for Testability (DFT) at the Unit Level: We ensure the design includes proper diagnostic interfaces so units can be verified for mission readiness efficiently, reliably and without destructive sealed-unit teardowns. Ensuring Operational Integration and Sovereign Requirements Plexus helps OEMs navigate the complexities of International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and Export Administration Regulations (EAR) through an integrated compliance framework. Our design and manufacturing facilities across the U.S., the UK and Europe provide the localized infrastructure required for advanced aerospace electronic manufacturing services while meeting specific sovereign capability goals. To meet specific sovereign capability goals and national content rules, we offer specialized regional support: North America: We leverage decades of defense experience and DoD Trusted Source Accreditation to support U.S. defense acquisition, ensuring that domestic production meets the highest standards of security and reliability. UK and Europe: We maintain ITAR-independent manufacturing capabilities that enable secure in-country production. This allows defence innovators to comply with Buy European or AUKUS directives regarding dual use military technology while mitigating the complexities of U.S. export regulations. By adhering to rigorous standards, we deliver the precision and material traceability required for high-integrity C-UAS hardware, whether building an anti drone jamming system or a kinetic interceptor platform: Certification Application Value to C-UAS AS9100 Aerospace Quality Management Ensures zero defects in harsh environments Nadcap Specialised Processes Accredits aerospace circuit board assembly JOSCAR Supplier Pre-qualification Eliminates administrative friction for MoD projects Cyber Essentials Plus IT Security Protects targeting algorithms and source code Because our global facilities operate with this unified system, we enable a copy exact transition once the necessary regulatory authorizations are in place. This ensures a solution matured in one region can be industrialized in another with process continuity and reliability. Partner with Plexus to Scale C-UAS Readiness Plexus serves as a trusted partner for global C-UAS OEMs, providing the scale and technical reliability required to meet global defense commitments. When mission success depends on closing the gap between a successful prototype and an interoperable, industrial-scale solution that meets the latest allied data standards, we provide the specialized engineering and manufacturing solutions needed to reach the field. title: Morningstar to Bring German Businesses Together in New Frankfurt Office in 2028
summary: New office at FOUR Frankfurt T1 will bring Morningstar's teams across its capabilities together in one location designed for future growth Frankfurt, Germany, 30 July 2026 – Morningstar, Inc. (Nasdaq: MORN), a leading provider of independent investing insights, today announced plans to move its Frankfurt office to FOUR Frankfurt T1 in 2028. The move reflects Morningstar's continued investment in Germany and helps reinforce Frankfurt's role as a key hub for its operations in Germany and across Eu
body_text: Media Hotline: +1 312 696-6037 newsroom@morningstar.com View All News Morningstar to Bring German Businesses Together in New Frankfurt Office in 2028 July 30, 2026 German (opens in new window) New office at FOUR Frankfurt T1 will bring Morningstar's teams across its capabilities together in one location designed for future growth Frankfurt, Germany, 30 July 2026 – Morningstar, Inc. (Nasdaq: MORN), a leading provider of independent investing insights, today announced plans to move its Frankfurt office to FOUR Frankfurt T1 in 2028. The move reflects Morningstar's continued investment in Germany and helps reinforce Frankfurt's role as a key hub for its operations in Germany and across Europe, bringing Morningstar's Germany-based employees together in one location for the first time. Teams across data, research and analytics from Morningstar Direct Platform; credit ratings from Morningstar DBRS; ESG data and ratings from Morningstar Sustainalytics; and indexes and benchmarks from Morningstar Indexes will be co-located across thoughtfully designed spaces tailored to their unique business requirements while supporting continued growth. Christian Mesenholl, managing director of central EMEA for Morningstar, said: "Our teams in Germany already work closely together for many of the same clients and markets. Bringing everyone together in one office can create more opportunities for innovation, and client engagement while supporting Morningstar's next stage of growth in Germany." Spanning floors 8 and 9 of FOUR Frankfurt T1, the new Morningstar Frankfurt office will provide modern, flexible workspaces designed around how people work today. The office will include dedicated collaboration spaces, quiet areas for focused work, and meeting and conference facilities for internal teamwork and client engagement. The larger footprint will also provide room for Morningstar's businesses in Germany to grow together in a single location. For clients, the office will provide a single Frankfurt location for meetings and engagement across Morningstar's full range of capabilities. Located in the heart of Frankfurt, FOUR Frankfurt T1 is part of the wider FOUR Frankfurt development, a mixed-use urban district that combines offices, residences, hotels, restaurants, retail, and public gathering spaces. The location is within walking distance of Hauptwache, Willy-Brandt-Platz, and Frankfurt's main shopping district, with direct access to public transportation. FOUR Frankfurt is pursuing DGNB Platinum certification, the highest certification awarded by the German Sustainable Building Council, for both the district and its individual towers. The development was also the first project in Germany to receive a DGNB Deconstruction Certificate, recognizing the reuse and recycling of materials from previous buildings on the site. The wider development incorporates geothermal energy, cycling infrastructure, and biodiversity-focused landscaping. Fast Facts What is Morningstar announcing? Morningstar plans to move its Frankfurt office to FOUR Frankfurt T1 in 2028. When is the move expected to occur? Morningstar expects to move in early 2028. Where will the new Morningstar Frankfurt office be located? FOUR Frankfurt T1, floors 8 and 9, Große Gallusstraße 14, Frankfurt am Main, Germany. Which teams will be located there? Teams across all Morningstar capabilities, including those from Morningstar Direct Platform, Morningstar DBRS, Morningstar Sustainalytics, and Morningstar Indexes. Why is Morningstar moving? To bring its German operations together in one location, while seeking to improve collaboration, enhance client engagement, and support future growth. Why does the location matter? The office is located in central Frankfurt with strong connections to clients and public transportation and is part of the mixed-use FOUR Frankfurt development. title: Pennsylvania American Water Awarded PENNVEST Funding Totaling $64+ Million for Water Infrastructure Improvement Projects in Allegheny, Cumberland and Susquehanna Counties
summary: Low-interest funding helps keep customer costs down while advancing water quality MECHANICSBURG, Pa., July 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Shapiro administration yesterday announced that Pennsylvania...
body_text: Low-interest funding helps keep customer costs down while advancing water quality MECHANICSBURG, Pa. , July 16, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- The Shapiro administration yesterday announced that Pennsylvania American Water was awarded grants and low-interest loans from the Pennsylvania Infrastructure Investment Authority (PENNVEST) totaling $64,106,000. The funding will support water infrastructure improvement projects in Allegheny, Cumberland and Susquehanna counties. "At Pennsylvania American Water, we strive to provide our customers with high-quality, reliable water and wastewater services while also meeting environmental standards and state and federal regulations. We're thankful to PENNVEST for approving our funding requests and supporting us in that mission," said the company's vice president of engineering, Tony Nokovich. "These projects will have a positive impact on the service provided for our customers by enabling us to continue our efforts to improve water and infrastructure across the state." A PENNVEST grant of $2,694,306 and loan of $6,205,694 will fund the replacement of approximately 575 identified lead and galvanized lead-impacted water service lines in Dormont Borough, Allegheny County. The removal of all leaded components will provide direct water quality improvements to customers and is consistent with regulatory and Pennsylvania American Water initiatives to eliminate lead-containing lines from the public water supply system. Learn more at pennsylvaniaamwater.com/leadfacts . The interest terms for the loan are 1.00% for the full 25.25-year loan period. "I am proud to have advocated for this funding and look forward to the positive impact it will make in Dormont," said Pennsylvania State Senator Wayne Fontana. "Clean water infrastructure continues to be a priority of mine and when the state can partner with organizations such as Pennsylvania American Water to make that happen, it is good for everyone." "This is an incredible investment for Dormont. Not only will it ensure that people have clean drinking water and infrastructure that will hold up for decades to come, but it will also protect residents from footing the bill of replacement, which is so important right now as costs are rising everywhere," said Pennsylvania State Representative Jen Mazzocco. In Cumberland County, a PFAS project to construct a new per- and polyfluoroalkyl (PFAS) treatment system at the company's Silver Spring Water Treatment Plant, which serves customers across 12 municipalities, received a PENNVEST grant of $2,447,879 and loan of $27,758,121. The proposed upgrades will install new granular activated carbon filter vessels designed to help ensure water meets U.S. Environmental Protection Agency PFAS regulations going into effect in 2029. It will also include additional pump, electrical, back-up power, security and stormwater improvements required as part of the new treatment system. The interest terms for the loan are 1.743% for the first five years and 2.179% for the remainder of the 20-year loan period. "Access to safe, reliable drinking water is absolutely essential," said Pennsylvania State Representative Thomas Kutz. "This $2.4 million state grant represents a significant investment in our community and in the roughly 85,000 people who depend on the Silver Spring Water Treatment Plant. I'm grateful to Pennsylvania American Water for its continued commitment to strengthening Cumberland County's water infrastructure and ensuring a dependable supply for generations to come." Pennsylvania American Water's Susquehanna Water Treatment Plant construction project in Harmony Township received a $25,000,000 PENNVEST loan. Due to the significant age, ongoing maintenance requirements and concerns related to the structural integrity of the existing plant's facilities, a new water treatment plant will be constructed on nearby company property to serve the system's more than 4,200 customers. The interest terms for the loan are 1.00% for the first five years and 1.743% for the remainder of the 20-year loan period. "Funding this project will ensure families in our community have safe, reliable drinking water by replacing aging infrastructure and modernizing treatment systems," said Pennsylvania State Senator Lisa Baker. "With PENNVEST's low‑interest financing, it delivers long-term health and affordability benefits for the 1,481 households who depend on this water supply." "Every Pennsylvanian has a constitutional right to pure water, and my Administration is continuing that work by investing in projects that modernize aging water infrastructure, replace lead service lines, and address contaminants like PFAS," said Governor Josh Shapiro in the Commonwealth's official announcement. "PENNVEST is helping communities across the Commonwealth make these critical upgrades so more Pennsylvanians have clean, safe, reliable drinking water when they turn on the tap." Since July 2024, PENNVEST has awarded Pennsylvania American Water more than $261.6 million in funding, including $29 million in grants and $231 million in low-interest loans to support statewide water and wastewater infrastructure projects. Learn more about this funding and how it helps the company reduce costs for its customers at pennsylvaniaamwater.com/pennvest . With a history dating back to 1886 and celebrating 140 years in 2026, We Keep Life Flowing® by providing safe, clean, reliable and affordable drinking water and wastewater services to approximately 14 million people with regulated operations in 14 states and on 18 military installations. American Water's approximately 7,000 talented professionals leverage their significant expertise and the company's national size and scale to achieve excellent outcomes for the benefit of customers, employees, investors and other stakeholders. title: From Year-End Filing to Micro Withholding: Africa's Move to Continuous Transaction Control
summary: As more African jurisdictions modernize their tax ecosystems, compliance is becoming a continuous operational function rather than a retrospective reporting exercise. In this environment, strong data governance, automated controls, and system integration are no longer competitive advantages; they are essential requirements for operating in an increasingly digital tax landscape.
body_text: The Post-Summary Reporting Era: Real-Time Transaction Validation Traditionally, the relationship between corporate taxpayers and African revenue authorities was largely retrospective. Businesses conducted their operations throughout the year with limited regulatory visibility, compiled their accounting records at month-end or year-end, and submitted summary tax returns based on historical transactions. Tax audits typically occurred months or even years after filing and relied heavily on manual reconciliations and sample testing. That model is rapidly disappearing across Africa. Revenue authorities are replacing traditional periodic reporting with Real-Time Transaction Validation (RTTV), embedding tax compliance directly into the transaction lifecycle. Instead of reviewing transactions after they occur, governments are increasingly requiring businesses to validate invoices, credit notes, and debit notes with tax authority systems at the moment they are created. Live API-Based Governance Across the continent, tax administrations are implementing Application Programming Interface (API) integrations that connect taxpayers' Point-of-Sale (POS), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and accounting systems directly to government platforms. Every qualifying transaction is transmitted electronically for validation before it becomes legally recognized. Once approved, the revenue authority issues a unique transaction identifier, cryptographic signature, QR code, or equivalent authentication token, which forms part of the official invoice. Without this validation, an invoice may be considered invalid for tax purposes, preventing customers from claiming input VAT or deductible business expenses. The Continental Transformation Although each jurisdiction has developed its own technological framework, the underlying principle is consistent: tax authorities increasingly rely on real-time transaction data as the primary source of compliance verification rather than taxpayer-prepared summaries. ‍ 1. Zimbabwe: TaRMS and FDMS Integration The Zimbabwe Revenue Authority (ZIMRA) has integrated its Tax and Revenue Management System (TaRMS) with the Fiscalisation Data Management System (FDMS), creating an automated compliance environment. Manual input tax schedules have been strictly outlawed. When a business logs into the portal to file its returns, the input tax module is pre-populated entirely by the system based on what suppliers have uploaded in real time. If a supplier fails to fiscalize an invoice, or if a physical QR code scanned by a customer shows as "Invalid," the buyer is legally barred from claiming the deduction. Zimbabwe's multi-currency environment also enables the system to capture transaction currencies at the point of sale, providing greater transparency over USD and Zimbabwe Gold (ZWG) transactions and reducing opportunities for post-period adjustments. 2. Zambia: Smart Invoice Implementation The Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA) has transitioned from traditional Electronic Fiscal Devices (EFDs) to its cloud-based Smart Invoice platform. Businesses using ERP systems, accounting software, or certified invoicing applications must transmit invoice data electronically for validation. Approved invoices receive a unique Mark ID together with a QR code that authenticates the transaction. Where invoices are generated during temporary internet outages, businesses are generally required to synchronize them within the statutory timelines. Failure to do so may result in penalties, while invoices lacking the required identifiers may not qualify for VAT or corporate income tax purposes. 3. Egypt: Pre-Validation of Electronic Invoices The Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) has adopted one of Africa's most advanced pre-validation models. Invoices generated by ERP or accounting systems are transmitted directly to the ETA in structured electronic formats before being delivered to customers. Following successful validation, the authority issues a unique Universal Unique Identifier (UUID), allowing the invoice to become legally recognized. Egypt has progressively expanded the scope of mandatory electronic invoicing and e-receipt requirements, bringing an increasing number of medium-sized enterprises, small businesses, and professionals into the real-time reporting framework. ‍ As more African jurisdictions modernize their tax ecosystems, compliance is becoming a continuous operational function rather than a retrospective reporting exercise. In this environment, strong data governance, automated controls, and system integration are no longer competitive advantages, they are essential requirements for operating in an increasingly digital tax landscape. ‍

title: Building Customer Value by Investing in Greif Plant Leadership
summary: At Greif, our ability to serve customers starts with the people leading our operations every day.
body_text: At Greif, our ability to serve customers starts with the people leading our operations every day. That is why Greif recently brought together nearly 200 Plant Managers from across our global manufacturing footprint for the first Plant Managers Forum in our company’s history. The purpose was to help make the best of Greif more consistent across every facility, every shift and every customer experience. Why Plant Leadership Matters in Manufacturing Strong plant leadership plays a critical role in delivering packaging quality, operational efficiency, workplace safety, and supply chain reliability. For manufacturers that depend on industrial packaging, effective plant management helps ensure products are produced consistently, delivered on time, and supported by continuous improvement initiatives. Strengthening Safety, Quality and Service Customers depend on Greif for packaging solutions that are safe, reliable and delivered to specifications. Meeting that expectation across a global business takes more than individual experience at a single location. It requires shared tools, disciplined processes and a consistent way to turn operational knowledge into better performance. The Greif Business System helps make that possible. It gives plant leaders a common approach for improving how work gets done, from identifying issues earlier to reducing waste and strengthening reliability through our sustainability and operational excellence initiatives. During the forum, Plant Managers spent time connecting these operational practices to customer outcomes. Discussions focused on value creation at the plant level, operational discipline, performance visibility and real examples of how value can be protected or lost in daily operations. The goal was not only to discuss what works. It was to help leaders take practical ideas back to their facilities and apply them in ways that improve performance for the customers we serve. More Than 2,200 Years of Operational Experience The forum also created space for plant leaders to learn from one another. Participants joined from across our Fiber packaging , Tambores de acero , polymer packaging, and closure solutions teams representing 40 countries and regions and more than 2,200 combined years of Greif experience. As a nearly 150-year-old company, that depth of knowledge is one of Greif’s strengths. Our plant leaders understand the products we make, the processes behind them and the expectations customers bring to every order. Many have built their expertise over decades on the plant floor and in operational leadership roles. Others bring fresh perspectives that help us continue challenging the way work gets done. When one facility finds a better way to reduce downtime, improve changeovers or strengthen quality, that knowledge should not stay in one place. Bringing plant leaders together helps proven practices move faster across the business and creates more opportunities to apply what is already working. Creating Customer Value Through One Greif For customers, the benefit is stronger operations behind every product and service Greif provides. The experience of our plant leaders, combined with the discipline of the Greif Business System, helps us improve how work gets done across our manufacturing footprint. That means better visibility, faster action and a continued focus on the quality and service customers expect from Greif. The first Plant Managers Forum reinforced what it means to operate as One Greif. It brought together the people who turn strategy into action, connect daily operations to customer needs and execute the systems that will help ensure Greif’s success today and for the next 150 years and beyond.
